reviews.author: Eva Boots
reviews.text: Route 20 is still closed just past the campground from the flooding in December, but the campground is open and in wonderful condition. The campsites are a little close but as long as you don't mind some noise from neighbors it's not an issue.

reviews.author: Francesc Vilariño Güell
reviews.text: Pretty nice campground to enjoy water activities on the lake, as well as some nearby hiking. The Diablo Lake trailhead is only 10 minutes driving and has good views of the lake and the dam. The campground has plenty of spots, but they vary significantly on size, some can only accommodate one small tent, while others have room for both a large tent and a small one. All spots have a dining table and fire pit, though fires are no longer allowed. The restroom is top notch, has running water and flushing toilets, magical! All in all, a great campground to relax and enjoy nature.

reviews.author: Anna
reviews.text:
This campsite is amazing!
We had no reservations and were relying on cancellations. We were blessed that weekend. Moved 3 times to different campsites that became available for that day. Rangers Wendy and Christine were awesome as well as the gentleman that opened up the camp for the day. No fees if you grab a cancelled site for the night. Please keep your food locked up either in your car or in storage that is provided at each site. Bears do come by and they recently had to put one down:/

reviews.author: daniel robinson
reviews.text: Beautiful camp ground with a gorgeous lake. This place is by far one of my favorite places. The sites are all sorts of sizes so please check in advance with recreation.gov to make sure your site will be what you need. The trails here are very well maintained and so is the beach. The water is very cold, gets deep quickly and has some very strong currents so please wear a life jacket at all times. Kayak and sup users be aware of the wind it picks up quick and tends to blow hard.

reviews.author: pacificnorthwestlandrover
reviews.text: love this location to stop at and take beautiful photos of Diablo and surroundings. camping spots with gorgeous views right on the water. i have yet to camp here, but looks like a great spot if you dont mind camping right next to a lot of people. restrooms, i hear have running water. each spot has lockable bear proof bins for your food

reviews.author: alexander f
reviews.text: I needed a site for the night before a weeklong backpacking trip but kind of forgot to plan that part. I was able to get a last minute site right on the lake, ~100ft walk from parking and it was just ...

reviews.author: Joan B
reviews.text: We camped in a tent area only. Quiet, clean with bear boxes and a picnic table at each site. Family friendly trailhead and more challenging hikes start right at the campground.

reviews.author: Matt Y
reviews.text: Wonderful experience! 148 was a decent but small campsite. It was very relaxing here! Hope to return!

reviews.author: Carol P
reviews.text: Site was great and bathroom was clean and stocked with toilet paper and soap. Thunder creek trail is lovely and shady along the creek with the trailhead in the campground.

reviews.author: Jacob K
reviews.text: Beautiful view, great location. A very memorable camping trip. Wish we could of had a camp fire but we came during the fire restrictions.

reviews.author: K O.
reviews.title: Fun N. Cascades Spot
reviews.text: Beautiful site! Try to get a reservation if you can, this campground can get really busy! Nice tent pads, and food storage lockers which is great. Like others mentioned, lots of winding trails nearby and the lake is amazing!

reviews.author: Shane D.
reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: pet friendly (on 6' leash), quiet, shaded. Clean bathrooms, but no showers. Fire ring, table, and bear proof cabinets at each site. surrounded by forest and on Diablo Lake! water is cold, but stunningly beautiful. some really nice hikes

reviews.author: Kylee A.
reviews.text: Get there early on a summer weekend. We arrived to the campsite Saturday around 11AM ($10/night). Each site had its own table and fire pit - ours was tucked into a nice private spot. Some of the sites had bear lockers and there were bathrooms nearby with running water and large trash bins throughout.

reviews.author: Al F
reviews.title: Wonderful mountain setting, beautiful lake, noisy traffic
reviews.text: Colonial Creek Campground is situated on the North Cascades Highway, on Diablo Lake. It is a wonderful mountain setting, along with the blue waters of the lake. Unfortunately, too many cars and large trucks rumble through at all hours of the day and night, making this a fairly noisy location, particularly given the setting. Most of the sites are good. It would pay to make an early reservation or get here early to get a more-coveted lakeside campsite. If you can, bring a kayak or a canoe, as this is a wonderful lake for exploring. In particular, we liked paddling across the lake, then up the narrow gorge leading toward the Ross Lake dam.

reviews.author: Sepehr Z.
reviews.text: A very beautiful place, calm, and gem place to camp. This camp ground has a long trail to enjoy between the woods and water. If you have plan to stay, just heads up, no internet and phone reception and might you meet bear!
